pr_title: Enhanced ACLK header payload to include timestamp-offset-usec
pr_body:
Fixes #8503
#### Summary
Added a new field in the ACLK header payload to include `timestamp-offset-usec`, that provides microseconds offset to the timestamp

##### Component Name
ACLK

##### Test Plan
- Agent with ACLK enabled
- All messages pushed to the cloud will have the header with the new field

issue_context.title: Enhance the ACLK JSON header with a new timestamp-offset-usec field
issue_context.body:
#### Summary

Add a new field to the ACLK JSON header `timestamp-offset-usec` that will provide microseconds offset to the `timestamp` in the range 0 ... 999999

Example:

Existing header

```
{ 
    "type": "status-change",
    "msg-id": "ef4b559e-6f01-4e00-95ff-adeff620d559",
    "timestamp": 1585240780,
    "version": 1,
    "payload": ...
}
```

new header 

```
{
    "type": "status-change",
    "msg-id": "ef4b559e-6f01-4e00-95ff-adeff620d559",
    "timestamp": 1585240780,
    "timestamp-offset-usec": 629572,
    "version": 1,
    "payload": ...
}
```

review_comments: Does using a function instead of repeating these 3 lines of code three times have a performance impact that is not negligible? I don't have any C expertise and I know the agent's code is higly optimized so I'm asking merely out of curiousity.

Good point @fracasula  but these 3 lines are used repeatedly only when building a header (with each message that goes to the cloud).

The other two occasions are on MQTT connect to define a LWT and when detecting a graceful shutdown to send a `graceful` message instead of `unexpected` (those two cases are rarely used)
